For photon–photon pair production the Lorentz–invariant energy is  

s = (p₁ + p₂)² = 2 E₁ E₂ (1 – cos θ) ,  

where θ is the angle between the two photons (E₁ ≡ Eγ for the high–energy photon and E₂ ≡ ε for the CMB photon).

Pair production becomes possible when the centre–of–mass energy equals the rest-mass energy of an electron–positron pair:

s ≥ (2 m_e c²)² = 4 m_e²c⁴.

The minimum Eγ occurs for a head-on collision (θ = π ⇒ 1 – cos θ = 2). Setting s = 4 m_e²c⁴ then gives  

2 Eγ ε (2) = 4 m_e²c⁴  ⇒  Eγ ε = m_e²c⁴.

Hence  

Eγ(threshold) = m_e²c⁴ / ε.

With  m_e c² = 0.511 MeV,  m_e²c⁴ = (0.511 MeV)² ≈ 0.261 MeV²,  
and the mean CMB photon energy ε ≈ 10⁻³ eV = 10⁻⁹ MeV,  

Eγ(threshold) ≈ 0.261 MeV² / 10⁻⁹ MeV ≈ 2.6 × 10⁸ MeV = 2.6 × 10⁵ GeV.

Therefore γ-rays with energies of order 2.6 × 10⁵ GeV (i.e. a few hundred TeV) will have their lifetimes limited by γγ → e⁺e⁻ interactions with the CMB.

Answer: B
